why: The hexagon has two rows of shapes (triangle, square, circle). The inside row moves one edge clockwise each step: top, upper right, lower right, bottom. The outside row moves one edge anticlockwise each step: top, upper left, lower left, bottom. Both rows meet again at the bottom in figure 4. So in the next figure the inside row goes to the lower left edge and the outside row goes to the lower right edge, with the order triangle, square, circle kept. Option 5 is wrong because its outside row has the order changed (square, circle, triangle). Options 2 and 4 are wrong because both rows sit on the same side.
trick: Track each group of shapes separately and note which way it moves, one edge per step. Then use the order of shapes inside each row to remove options.
note: Original shape order and tilt in figure 4 is not an exact rotation, so the rule is inferred. Option 3 is the only one with inside row lower-left and outside row lower-right with correct shape order.
